notes.10: This was one of the most demanding questions on the paper. Candidates were required to recall the electrode products in two different electrolysis reactions. All the options were popular. Option C was most commonly chosen by candidates who performed less well.

notes.17: Candidates often find bond enthalpy questions difficult. A number of candidates chose option B. This answer has the opposite sign to the correct answer, suggesting that candidates confused the sign of energy changes during bond breaking and bond forming.
notes.21: Option B was a common incorrect answer. Candidates may have confused typical properties of transition elements with Group I elements.
notes.22: This question was one of the more demanding questions on the paper. Most candidates chose option B. Candidates predicted helium would have eight outer shell electrons which is incorrect.
notes.27: The most common answer was option B. Candidates should recall that oxides of nitrogen cause acidic rain whereas carbon monoxide is a neutral oxide.
notes.29: Slightly fewer candidates chose option A, but all the other options were as likely to be chosen as each other, suggesting guessing by many candidates. Candidates who performed least well were more likely to choose option C.
notes.30: Most candidates were unable to recall the catalyst used in the Contact process. All options were chosen, with option C being most commonly given.
notes.34: This was one of the more challenging questions, with almost a third of candidates choosing option B, confusing oxidation with dehydration.
